# GCTRL

> GCTRL (Ground Control) is the enterprise memory layer for AI: a self-hosted knowledge graph and governed memory tier that ingests unstructured organizational data, resolves it into one clean graph, and serves it to any agent framework as durable, access-controlled shared memory - running fully on-prem, with local inference, no vendor lock-in, and no per-token cost.

GCTRL sits between an organization's raw data (documents, mail servers, SharePoint, SQL databases, file shares) and its AI agents. Instead of every coding agent, copilot, or automation rebuilding its own understanding of the company from scratch, they all read and write to the same governed knowledge graph - what one agent learns is already there when the next one asks.

## Core capabilities

- **KEX (Knowledge Extraction)** - turns unstructured documents into structured entities and relations, locally and fast.
- **FUSE (Knowledge Fusion)** - merges extractions and resolves duplicate/conflicting entities into one coherent graph, with zero training required.
- **Classification & Access Control** - clearance enforced on every graph read, scoped tokens for per-project or per-agent isolation.
- **Multi-Agent Fabric** - one governed memory layer exposed over MCP and HTTP to every agent framework (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, LangChain, LlamaIndex, n8n, and more).
- **Cloaking** - use frontier cloud models without exposing real identities in the data sent upstream.
- **Sovereign & On-Prem** - every component (graph, vectors, relational store, queue, inference) runs on infrastructure you control; deployments can go fully air-gapped.
- **Talk to Graph** - grounded, cited, GDPR-compliant chat over your own knowledge graph.

- [How to Fill Time Gaps Irregular Timestamps Pandas Guide](https://gctrl.tech/blog/how-to-fill-gaps-in-irregular-time-series-data): Learn how to fill time gaps irregular timestamps pandas workflows using resample, reindex, and interpolation to standardize your time series data.
- [How to Improve Basic FAISS RAG Pipeline Performance](https://gctrl.tech/blog/beyond-basic-faiss-optimizing-your-rag-retrieval-pipeline): Learn how to improve basic faiss rag pipeline results using recursive chunking, retrieval gates, and RAGAS evaluations to stop hallucinations.
- [Best Tools for LLM Product Analytics: Evals and Monitoring](https://gctrl.tech/blog/llm-product-analytics-the-stack-for-evals-and-monitoring): Discover the best tools for llm product analytics. Learn how to use Confident AI, DeepEval, and Langfuse for pre-production evals and production monitoring.
- [Entity Resolution Duplicate Names: Improving RAG Accuracy](https://gctrl.tech/blog/entity-resolution-for-rag-merging-duplicate-identities-in-knowle): Learn how entity resolution duplicate names prevents retrieval fragmentation and hallucinations in RAG systems by merging records into a golden record.
- [How to Build Knowledge Graph from Documents for Your Company](https://gctrl.tech/blog/how-to-build-a-company-knowledge-graph-from-unstructured-documents): Learn how to build knowledge graph from documents using a four-stage pipeline to improve multi-hop reasoning and entity relationship extraction.
- [EU AI Act for RAG Deployments: What Actually Applies Since August 2026](https://gctrl.tech/blog/eu-ai-act-rag-deployments-2026): Article 50 transparency is enforceable since 2 August 2026, while high-risk duties moved to 2027. A practical checklist for teams running RAG and AI memory in the EU.
- [The Real Cost of Metered AI Memory (and Why We Refuse to Count Tokens)](https://gctrl.tech/blog/unlimited-tokens-metered-ai-memory): Cloud memory platforms charge around $2.50 per million tokens after a small free grant. The arithmetic looks harmless - until you run a real team's workload through it.
- [Self-Hosted RAG in 2026: Why Serious Teams Are Moving On-Prem](https://gctrl.tech/blog/self-hosted-rag-on-prem-guide): Data sovereignty, predictable cost, and EU compliance are pushing RAG workloads back on-prem. What self-hosting actually takes, and what you get for it.
- [GraphRAG vs. Vector RAG: When a Knowledge Graph Beats Top-k](https://gctrl.tech/blog/graphrag-vs-vector-rag): Vector search answers "what sounds similar" - a knowledge graph answers "what is actually connected". Where plain RAG breaks, and when GraphRAG is worth it.
